results.title: PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk (EMTK) strengthens its position in PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (BUKA) and PT Nitrasanata Dharma Tbk (JECX)
results.body: The BEI disclosed on 22 Sep that PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk (EMTK) increased its holdings in PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (BUKA) by 188.70 million shares, raising its stake to 10.67%, and added 1.17 million shares of PT Nitrasanata Dharma Tbk (JECX) through its health subsidiary PT Sarana Meditama Metropolitan Tbk (SAME), bringing its total shareholdings to 33%. PT Yulie Sekuritas Indonesia Tbk (YULE) raised its stake in PT Esa Medika Mandiri Tbk (EMMI) to about 10.19%; Samudra (Investment) Pte. Ltd boosted its holding in PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk (MAPI) to 30.19%; and Lo Kheng Hong increased his position in PT Intiland Development Tbk (DILD) to 7.54%. Edwin Soeryadjaya now controls 35.95% of PT Saratoga Investama Sedaya Tbk (SRTG), Ferry Sudjono holds roughly 6.02% of PT Fore Kopi Indonesia Tbk (FORE), while Dato Tahir reduced his stake in PT Maha Properti Indonesia Tbk (MPRO) to 10.46%. PT Global Mediacom Tbk (BMTR) sold 28.90 million shares of its subsidiary PT Media Nusantara Citra Tbk (MNCN), lowering its control to 38.23%, and The Bank of New York Mellon divested 6 million shares of PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM), retaining about 6.3% of the telecom firm.

results.title: Emtek subsidiary PT Kreatif Media Karya acquires 803.28 million shares of PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, raising its stake to 45.68%
results.body: On Tuesday, 8 September, PT Kreatif Media Karya, an Emtek subsidiary, purchased 803.28 million shares of PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, increasing its ownership to 45.68%. The same filing shows Lo Kheng Hong buying 1 million shares of PT Intiland Development Tbk, lifting his holding to 7.51%, and Edwin Soeryadjaya acquiring 600 thousand shares of PT Saratoga Investama Sedaya Tbk, maintaining a 35.9% stake. Buyback actions were noted for PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (781,700 shares, 5.63% ownership), PT United Tractors Tbk (1.01 million shares, 7.77% ownership) and PT Arwana Citramulia Tbk (200,000 shares, 5.16% ownership). Additionally, CGS International Securities Singapore Pte Ltd sold 126 million shares of PT Wilton Makmur Indonesia Tbk, reducing its stake to 18.77%, while PT Bahana Nusantara Indojaya and PT Nusantara Makmur Lestari sold 2.55 million shares of PT Indokripto Koin Semesta Tbk (remaining 19.62%) and 205 thousand shares of PT Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera Tbk (remaining 9.46%) respectively.

results.title: Rd Adi Wardhana Sariaatmadja Buy Shares of Bukalapak.com
results.body: Insider Rd Adi Wardhana Sariaatmadja purchased 635,000,000 Bukalapak.com shares at IDR 124 per share on September 4, 2026, for a total of IDR 78,740,000,000. The acquisition increased his holding from 772,585,501 shares (0.841%) to 1,407,585,501 shares (1.533%). The purpose was investment.

results.title: Grup Emtek Strengthens Bukalapak Stake, Purchases 803 Million Shares at Above-Market Price
results.body: PT Kreatif Media Karya (KMK Online), a digital subsidiary of PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk (EMTK), has increased its stake in PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (BUKA) by purchasing 803,287,800 shares on 4 September 2026. The shares were bought at Rp126 each, totaling Rp101,214 million, which is above BUKA's closing price of Rp113 per share on the same day. The acquisition raised KMK Online's ownership of BUKA to 45.68% from 44.90%, strengthening its control over the e‑commerce platform.

results.title: PT Kreatif Media Karya increases its stake in PT Bukalapak.com Tbk to 45.68%
results.body: PT Kreatif Media Karya, the controlling shareholder of PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, increased its ownership to 45.68% by buying additional shares. On 4 September 2026 it purchased 803,287,800 shares at Rp126 each, costing about Rp101.21 billion and raising its holding to 47,125,034,185 shares out of 46,321,746,385 total shares. The filing also shows that PT Elang Mahkota and PT Bukalapak each hold over 10% of PT Bukalapak.com Tbk’s shares, with 10,821,706,040 (10.48%) and 11,333,437,507 (10.986%) shares respectively. Following the transaction, PT Bukalapak.com Tbk’s shares closed at 113 on 7 September, down 1.74% (‑2 points), and the stock carries a special notation I.

results.title: Kreatif Media Karya Buy Shares of Bukalapak.com
results.body: Insider Kreatif Media Karya purchased 803,287,800 Bukalapak.com shares at IDR 126 per share, a transaction worth IDR 101,214,262,800, increasing its holding to 47,125,034,185 shares and raising its ownership from 44.90% to 45.68% as an investment move.

results.title: Foreign investors heavily buy big bank stocks PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk in the past week.
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors returned to Indonesia’s banking sector last week, posting the largest net purchases in the market for the three big banks. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk recorded a net buy of Rp 1.41 trillion, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk Rp 1.20 trillion and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk Rp 1.01 trillion, together accounting for about Rp 3.62 trillion of foreign inflows, while PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk added Rp 261.39 billion. Other heavily bought stocks included PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp 238.84 billion), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (Rp 168.05 billion), PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (Rp 147.58 billion), PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk (Rp 126.94 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 93.49 billion) and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (Rp 84.23 billion). Foreign investors sold PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (Rp 485.66 billion), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (Rp 337.42 billion), PT Indosat Tbk (Rp 225.62 billion), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (Rp 173 billion), PT Petrosea Tbk (Rp 162.7 billion), PT Astra International Tbk (Rp 150.28 billion), PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (Rp 129.03 billion), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (Rp 126.97 billion), PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (Rp 121.57 billion) and PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk (Rp 109.91 billion), contributing to a total foreign net buy of Rp 1.85 trillion and supporting a 1.82 % weekly rise in the IHSG index, which closed at 6,636.47, down 31.4 points (0.47 %) on Friday.

results.title: Analysts highlight stocks to watch as MSCI and FTSE Russell rebalancing looms over September 2026 Indonesian market
results.body: The upcoming MSCI rebalancing on 1 September and FTSE Russell rebalancing on 21 September are expected to increase volatility in the Indonesian IHSG. Analysts note that foreign fund inflows in August reached roughly Rp10 trillion and that the FTSE Russell adjustments can be revised until 4 September, making the technical pressure likely temporary. Directly affected companies include PT Bank Central Asia Tbk., PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk., ARTO, BUKA, ESSA, FILM, HEAL, KPIG, RATU, SMGR and TCPI, which may face sell pressure after MSCI exclusions, as well as BSDE, BBYB, BJBR, BTPS, LPKR, LPPF, MNCN, PNLF, SILO, SMRA and SCMA, slated to drop to lower FTSE Russell caps and potentially lose passive demand. The analysts advise a prudent approach, waiting for technical pressure to subside while monitoring rupiah stability and broader macro‑economic factors.

results.title: MSCI Rebalancing Takes PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia, PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia and Nine Small‑Cap Stocks Out of Indexes
results.body: The article reports that MSCI’s upcoming rebalancing, effective 31 August 2026, will remove PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk and PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk from the Global Standard and nine stocks—ARTO, BUKA, ESSA, FILM, HEAL, KPIG, RATU, SMGR and TCPI—from the MSCI Small‑Cap index. Phintraco Sekuritas projects the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) to trade in a narrow consolidation range of 6,400 to 6,600 during the next week, noting the index closed at 6,518.12 on 28 August 2026, down 0.06% and having corrected 0.12% for the week. The research team highlights that the rebalancing could increase volatility for the affected stocks, while investors will also watch domestic economic releases on 1 September 2026, including PMI Manufacturing, trade balance and inflation data. Historically, September tends to be a volatile month, prompting a more cautious stance among market participants.

results.title: Kiwoom Sekuritas warns of sell pressure on MSCI‑removed Indonesian stocks and issues a buy recommendation for PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk
results.body: MSCI index rebalancing effective 31 August 2026 is expected to create sell pressure on Indonesian stocks removed from the index. Bloomberg estimates passive outflows of about US$753 million, with US$684 million from Standard‑Cap stocks and US$68 million from Small‑Cap stocks; PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk faces the largest outflow of roughly US$407 million, while PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk has a net outflow of about US$127 million after a US$50 million inflow, and PT Bank Jago Tbk, PT Medikaloka Hermina Tbk, PT Semen Indonesia Tbk and PT Bukalapak.com Tbk are also flagged for potential pressure, whereas PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk could receive passive inflows. In the first half of 2026 PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk reported net profit of Rp607 billion, PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk posted Rp3.7 trillion net profit (+95 % YoY), and PT Medikaloka Hermina Tbk saw net profit fall 14 % to Rp193 billion. Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia therefore issues a buy recommendation on PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk with a target price of Rp3,150 per share.

results.title: Stocks Impacted by MSCI Rebalancing Face Potential Pressure; Analyst Recommendations Reviewed
results.body: The article discusses the upcoming MSCI index rebalancing effective after the close of trading on 31 August 2026, which is expected to create sell pressure on several Indonesian stocks. The rebalancing removes PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk from the MSCI Global Standard, moves PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk from the MSCI Global Standard to the MSCI Global Small Cap, and drops PT Bank Jago Tbk, PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, PT Surya Esa Perkasa Tbk, PT Medikaloka Hermina Tbk, PT Raharja Energi Cepu Tbk, PT Semen Indonesia Tbk, and PT Transcoal Pacific Tbk from the MSCI Global Small Cap. Analyst Hendra Wardana recommends a wait‑and‑see stance for PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk with the stock near Rp 50, a speculative‑buy target of Rp 1,640 for PT Semen Indonesia Tbk, and sell‑on‑strength targets of Rp 2,200 for PT Transcoal Pacific Tbk, Rp 98 for PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, Rp 905 for PT Bank Jago Tbk, Rp 575 for PT Surya Esa Perkasa Tbk, Rp 600 for PT Medikaloka Hermina Tbk, and Rp 4,500 for PT Raharja Energi Cepu Tbk. The analyst notes that the pressure stems from passive‑index investors adjusting portfolios, but it does not imply a deterioration of the companies’ fundamentals. The rebalancing announcement was first made on 12 August 2026, and the potential sell pressure may persist through the end of August 2026.

results.title: Short‑Term IHSG Outlook Highlights Upcoming MSCI Index Rebalancing and Expected Volatility
results.body: The article discusses the short‑term projection for Indonesia’s composite index (IHSG) ahead of the MSCI index rebalancing that becomes effective at the close of trading on 31 August 2026 (opening 1 September 2026). MSCI will remove GOTO and CPIN from the Global Standard category and will drop nine small‑cap stocks—ARTO, BUKA, ESSA, FILM, HEAL, KPIG, RATU, SMGR and TCPI—from the Small Cap category, prompting expected passive‑fund outflows and heightened volume and volatility through 29‑31 August. Analyst Hendry Wijaya projects IHSG support between 6,377 and 6,255 and resistance between 6,623 and 6,730, with technical pressure easing after 1 September, while Kiwoom analyst Azis forecasts sideways movement and possible foreign‑flow‑driven swings. The commentary also notes a stronger rupiah at roughly Rp 17,670 per USD and target‑price recommendations for BBCA (Rp 8,075) and BMRI (Rp 5,400), but the core market impact centers on the listed MSCI‑removed stocks.

results.title: IHSG projection ahead of MSCI rebalancing with analyst‑selected stock outlook
results.body: The article discusses the analyst’s projection for Indonesia’s IHSG index as the MSCI August 2026 rebalancing approaches. It notes that the index slipped 0.37% to 6,501 and is trading near 6,420, with support levels at 6,377‑6,255 and resistance at 6,623‑6,730, while volume and volatility are expected to peak on August 29‑31 as passive funds adjust. The rebalancing will remove PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk and PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk from the MSCI Global Standard and will also drop nine stocks—PT Bank Jago Tbk, PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, PT ESSA Industries Indonesia Tbk, PT MD Pictures Tbk, PT Medikaloka Hermina Tbk, PT MNC Land Tbk, PT Raharja Energi Cepu Tbk, PT Semen Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, and PT Transcoal Pacific Tbk—from the MSCI Small Cap index, exposing them to potential sell pressure. The analyst expects the technical pressure to subside after the August 31 effective date, after which IHSG direction will be driven by macro fundamentals and global sentiment.

results.title: Upcoming MSCI Index Rebalancing Ahead of Week, Projected Direction for Indonesia's IHSG
results.body: The article discusses the MSCI index rebalancing scheduled for the close of trading on 31 August 2026 (effective 1 September 2026) and its expected influence on Indonesia’s composite index (IHSG). In this rebalancing, GOTO and CPIN are removed from the Global Standard category, while ARTO, BUKA, ESSA, FILM, HEAL, KPIG, RATU, SMGR and TCPI are taken out of the Small‑Cap category. Analysts from Sucor Sekuritas and Kiwoom Sekuritas anticipate heightened trading volume and volatility through 29‑31 August, with IHSG support projected at 6,377–6,255 and resistance at 6,623–6,730. They also note that passive‑fund outflows may affect the delisted stocks, while sectors such as commodities and energy, and stocks like AMMN, PSAB, BRMS, INET, BUMI, PTRO, PGEO and TINS could attract attention after the technical pressure eases. Additional domestic and global macro factors, including the Bank Indonesia governor test, rupiah levels, US PCE data and Fed policy signals, are cited as background influences but not the primary driver.

results.title: MSCI removes 10 Indonesian stocks, all tumble on Thursday
results.body: MSCI announced that ten Indonesian equities were removed from its Global Standard Indexes, with one shifted to the Global Small Cap Index, prompting a uniform decline on Thursday 13 August 2026. The affected issuers – PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Jago Tbk, PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, PT ESSA Industries Indonesia Tbk, PT MD Intertainment Tbk, PT Medikaloka Hermina Tbk, PT MNC Tourism Indonesia Tbk, PT Raharja Energi Cepu Tbk, PT Semen Indonesia Tbk and PT Transcoal Pacific Tbk – fell between 2.5 % and 8.8 %, with PT MD Intertainment Tbk down 8.82 % to Rp 930 and PT ESSA Industries Indonesia Tbk down 7.04 % to Rp 660. Prices for the stocks ranged from Rp 50 for PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk to Rp 3 560 for PT Transcoal Pacific Tbk. MSCI said the changes will take effect at the close of trading on 31 August 2026.

results.title: MSCI August 2026 review deletes 13 Indonesian stocks while foreign investors net‑sell Rp1.41 trillion
results.body: The article reports that during MSCI’s August 2026 index review, the provider removed 13 Indonesian companies from its Global Standard and Global Small‑Cap indexes. Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp1.41 trillion on the Jakarta market on Thursday 13 August 2026, with the largest single‑stock outflow in PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp183.86 billion) and the stock falling 4.63 % to Rp2,060. The biggest net purchase was in PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, where foreign investors bought Rp129.42 billion of shares, lifting the price 0.39 % to Rp6,375. The deletions include PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk and PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk from the MSCI Global Standard Indexes, and PT Bank Jago Tbk, PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, PT ESSA Industries Indonesia Tbk, PT MD Entertainment Tbk, PT Medikaloka Hermina Tbk, PT MNC Tourism Indonesia Tbk, PT Raharja Energi Cepu Tbk, PT Semen Indonesia Tbk and PT Transcoal Pacific Tbk from the MSCI Global Small‑Cap Indexes.

results.title: MSCI Keeps Indonesia in Emerging‑Market Category While Removing Ten Indonesian Stocks from Its Indexes Effective Aug 31 2026
results.body: MSCI announced that Indonesia remains classified as an Emerging Market in its MSCI Frontier Emerging Markets Index, putting it on par with Malaysia, China and other countries. The annual country review indicated no change to the list of Emerging Market countries. However, MSCI will remove ten Indonesian equities from its global indexes effective at the close of trading on 31 August 2026. The removals include PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk from the MSCI Global Standard Indexes, PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk shifting to the MSCI Global Small Cap Indexes, and nine other stocks – PT Bank Jago Tbk, PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, PT ESSA Industries Indonesia Tbk, PT MD Intertainment Tbk, PT Medikaloka Hermina Tbk, PT MNC Tourism Indonesia Tbk, PT Raharja Energi Cepu Tbk, PT Semen Indonesia (Persero) Tbk and PT Transcoal Pacific Tbk – being taken out of the MSCI Global Small Cap Indexes. All changes will take effect after market close on 31 August 2026.

results.title: Investor Confidence Weakens During Prabowo Administration as MSCI Removes 11 Indonesian Stocks, IHSG Could Slip Below 6,000
results.body: The article notes that investor confidence in Indonesia’s equity market has weakened during President Prabowo Subianto’s term, highlighted by MSCI’s latest rebalancing actions. MSCI kept Indonesia in the emerging‑market group but maintained a freeze on new weightings and downgraded PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk’s classification from Global Standard to Small Cap. It also removed PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk and nine other issuers—Bank Jago, Bukalapak.com, Essa Industries Indo, MD Entertainment, Medikaloka Hermina, MNC Tourism Indonesia, Raharja Energi Cepu, Semen Indonesia, and Transcoal Pacific—from the MSCI Indonesia Investable Market Index or MSCI Global Small Cap lists, effective 31 August 2026. The commentary cites a 27.12 % year‑to‑date decline in the IHSG, a 7.09 % depreciation of the rupiah against the US dollar, and foreign outflows of IDR 95.17 trillion, while noting a modest US$88 million foreign equity inflow in July. Analysts project the IHSG could trade between 6,500 and 7,000 by year‑end, but a further drop below 6,000 remains possible if MSCI’s November decisions or macro risks worsen.

results.title: MSCI Keeps Indonesia in Emerging Markets but Removes Ten Local Stocks, Prompting Potential Passive Outflows
results.body: MSCI reaffirmed Indonesia's Emerging Market classification while reshuffling its index constituents. GOTO was removed from the MSCI Global Standard and Indonesia Investable Market indexes due to liquidity concerns, CPIN was shifted to the Global Small Cap index, and nine other stocks – ARTO, BUKA, ESSA, FILM, HEAL, KPIG, RATU, SMGR and TCPI – were dropped from the Global Small Cap index. The changes become effective after market close on 31 August 2026 and will be reflected in trading on 1 September 2026. Mirae Asset Sekuritas estimates passive outflows of roughly Rp500 billion to Rp1 trillion, and Indonesia's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets index is expected to fall from about 0.49 % to 0.46 %. Analysts say the removals highlight liquidity and investability challenges for the Indonesian market.

results.title: Several Indonesian Stocks Removed from MSCI Indices: Outlook Ahead
results.body: The article discusses the removal of a group of Indonesian equities from MSCI’s August 2026 index review, highlighting the implications for their future performance. PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk was taken out of the MSCI Global Standard Index, PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk was shifted to the Small‑Cap category, and PT Bank Jago Tbk, PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, PT ESSA Industries Tbk, PT MD Entertainment Tbk, PT Medikaloka Hermina Tbk, PT MNC Tourism Indonesia Tbk, PT Raharja Energi Cepu Tbk, PT Semen Indonesia Tbk and PT Transcoal Pacific Tbk were removed from the MSCI Small‑Cap Index. Analyst Sukarno Alatas notes that despite ESSA’s removal, its revenue grew 36% year‑on‑year and net profit more than doubled year‑on‑year in the first half of 2026, supported by a 27% YTD rise in Middle‑East ammonia prices to about US$795 per ton, and he recommends a trading‑buy target of Rp700‑Rp735. Hendra Wardana cautions that the rebalancing pressure is technical and may cause short‑term price declines, but companies with strong fundamentals and adequate liquidity could recover once the effect subsides. The commentary stresses that market‑cap size alone does not guarantee investability; free‑float, liquidity and transparent governance remain key for attracting global investors.
